title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers used AI-generated videos and text to impersonate a real immigration attorney on social media, creating hundreds of fake profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram. This was an impersonation attack that exploited the attorney's identity and reputation to commit fraud, targeting a vulnerable population seeking immigration services. The system deployed was social media hosting without sufficient verification that accounts offering legal services were legitimate.

The fraud worked because social media platforms did not block accounts making false claims about legal credentials or requiring payment for immigration assistance before the attorney's office hired an outside firm to remove them. Catching this would have required platforms to verify the identity of accounts offering regulated services like immigration law, or to flag accounts using AI-generated video of real people without consent. It is not established whether social media companies received reports about the fraud before the attorney's office engaged external help.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience says criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. Angel Leal discovered that scammers created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos of him offering immigration services he never provides, including false promises of US residency for $2,200. The scheme escalated dramatically in recent months after potential clients began calling his office about these fraudulent offers.

To combat the fraud, Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically start with social media videos directing victims to contact a WhatsApp number, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect payments through apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the source of the scams. He advises immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to be suspicious of social media ads promising immigration benefits for immediate payment.
